items.title: 67426_Hayes Pillars oral history interview
items.q: I should never forget when I first met Claude Hopkins... I met Claude Hopkins when he called himself the Six Gingersnaps... That was back in 1927.

ctx.x: And Jonah Jones George Owens, and another fella that -- that played -- that played in and around there, Dick Wells. Trombone player, you may know of him? And you may not. Dick Wells. There was another band out of Springfield, Ohio, that used to play through Cincinnati, into Louisville, and this band was Cecil Scott. Had a brother named Lloyd Scott. Cecil Scott was a baritone saxophone player, he was a terrific musician. They Tell me he jumped out of a window or something in New York and he broke one of his legs…

I mentioned Speed Webb, you know, and -- the -- Teddy Wilson and those guys, worked in the band. You know, back in 1927, we would go and play dances in Indianapolis, Indiana. And there was a little nightclub there, where they would, you know, hired bands and I should never forget when I first met Claude Hopkins, you know Claude Hopkins, don't you? The band leader? Claude Hopkins?
